results.answer:
Southwest's 87 737 MAX 8 aircraft were all operating with MCAS v1.7.3 as of January 1, 2024, and FAA AD 2024-01-02 requires installation of MCAS v2.0 or later by May 15, 2024. The fleet was compliant with FAA AD 2020-05-11 (pre-service compliance November 2020) and FAA AD 2022-03-07 (completed April 2022). Software updates to v2.0 were scheduled February-May 2024 on a phased basis (~10 aircraft/month).

For the specific aircraft G-ABCD, the current software is MCAS v1.7.3 versus the required v2.0 or later, and the status is recorded as non-compliant with the compliance deadline not yet reached; the aircraft remains airworthy under v1.7.3 until the May 15, 2024 deadline, with installation scheduled April 22-23, 2024 per Boeing Service Bulletin Revision 2.

Under 14 CFR Part 39, operators of 737-8 and 737-9 aircraft are legally required to comply with all applicable ADs, and non-compliance renders the aircraft unairworthy for operation under FAA jurisdiction.
